history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 655 ('Shri Hanuman Thakur Temple', CSV town Chandel — town almost certainly wrong; file 655 identifies the same Mahabali, Imphal temple). The Shree Hanuman Thakur Temple stands on the banks of the Imphal River in the Mahabali forest groves (Wangkhei, Imphal East). Built in 1725 AD by King Garib Niwaj (Pamheiba), it is reportedly the only temple constructed during his reign and a monument to the spread of the Ramanandi cult of Hinduism in Manipur — a cult that faded after his death. It is built in the hut-type Bengal style: a brick structure (later cement-plastered), with a hemispherical domed sanctum, double-lotus criss-cross crown, kalasas and a vase bearing the Nilchakra. The presiding idol is Hanuman shown in human form, carved out of a single big slab of stone.

town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur, set in the flat Imphal Valley at about 786 m and ringed by hills. It is the historic seat of the Meitei kings — Kangla Fort, the former royal palace and the Govindajee temple stand at its centre — and the heart of Manipuri Vaishnavite culture, classical dance and handloom. The city is Manipur's road and air hub, served by Bir Tikendrajit International Airport and national highways to Nagaland, Assam and Myanmar.
